subs.label: Drama
subs.axis: Axis: by the dramatic engine — the bond, inner state, social condition, institution, contest or journey the drama turns on: family and home first, then the self, youth, society and its institutions, faith, sport, and journeys and animals last.

leaves.label: Shomingeki (Shoshimin-eiga)
leaves.defn: A Japanese studio drama of ordinary lower-middle-class urban life: salarymen, households, marriages arranged and parents left behind, told at the scale of the home (Tokyo Story, Late Spring, I Was Born, But...). Non-Japanese family dramas go to A16-3 or A16-4.
leaves.see: A16-4 Parent–Child Drama; A1 Movements & Schools

leaves.label: Family Saga
leaves.defn: A drama that follows one family across generations or decades, the passing of time and inheritance of fortune being the engine (The Magnificent Ambersons, Giant, Fanny and Alexander, The Best of Youth). A drama confined to one crisis in one generation goes to A16-3 or A16-4.
leaves.see: A16-3 Family Drama; A8 Historical & Period Film

leaves.label: Family Drama
leaves.defn: A drama whose engine is the family as a group rather than one parent–child pair: siblings, the family gathered for a holiday or funeral, the inheritance, the household after a death, the chosen or foster family (Still Walking, Rachel Getting Married, Shoplifters, Ordinary People). One parent and child at the centre goes to A16-4; a couple to A16-5.
leaves.see: A16-4 Parent–Child Drama; A16-5 Domestic Drama; A16-2 Family Saga
leaves.axis: by the family bond in play: siblings first, then the gathered family, the inheritance, the bereaved household, and found or foster families last

leaves.label: Parent–Child Drama
leaves.defn: A drama centred on one parent and child — the father–son or mother–daughter bond strained, broken or repaired (The Return, Aftersun, Autumn Sonata, Mommy, On Golden Pond). A drama of the whole family goes to A16-3; Japanese shomingeki to A16-1.
leaves.see: A16-3 Family Drama; A16-13 Coming-of-Age Film
leaves.axis: by which parent and child: fathers and sons, fathers and daughters, mothers and children, then ageing parents and their adult children

leaves.label: Domestic Drama
leaves.defn: A drama of the married couple at home — the marriage worn down, betrayed or dissolved (Scenes from a Marriage, Revolutionary Road, Kramer vs. Kramer, Marriage Story). A romance that ends in marriage goes to A13; the wider family to A16-3.
leaves.see: A13 Romance; A16-3 Family Drama; A16-6 Melodrama
leaves.axis: by the state of the marriage: the marriage in crisis, adultery, then divorce and custody

leaves.label: Melodrama
leaves.defn: A drama in the melodramatic mode — heightened emotion, sacrifice and fate carried by music and mise-en-scène, usually centred on a suffering woman or family (Stella Dallas, All That Heaven Allows, Imitation of Life, All About My Mother). Realist family dramas go to A16-3 to A16-5.
leaves.see: A16-5 Domestic Drama; A13 Romance
leaves.axis: by the sacrifice at the core: maternal sacrifice first, then the woman's film of the fallen or desiring woman, the family melodrama, and the illness tearjerker last

leaves.label: Psychological Drama
leaves.defn: A drama whose engine is one person's inner state — grief, breakdown, trauma or obsession — rendered from inside (Three Colors: Blue, Through a Glass Darkly, Manchester by the Sea, Death in Venice). Where suspense drives it, see A3; where the crisis is existential rather than psychological, A16-8.
leaves.see: A16-8 Existentialist Film; A3 Thriller & Mystery; A16-26 Medical Drama
leaves.axis: by the inner condition: grief first, then breakdown and mental illness, trauma and guilt, and obsession last

leaves.label: Existentialist Film
leaves.defn: An art-film character study whose engine is a crisis of meaning — alienation, ennui, a life weighed up or a self disguised (La Dolce Vita, The Silence, Lost in Translation, The Passenger, Citizen Kane). A clinical inner state goes to A16-7; a quiet everyday portrait to A16-9.
leaves.see: A16-7 Psychological Drama; A16-9 Slice of Life; A1 Movements & Schools
leaves.axis: by the shape of the crisis: modernist alienation, the ennui of the affluent, double lives and masks, rise-and-fall lives, then midlife and old age

leaves.label: Slice of Life
leaves.defn: A drama with no plot engine beyond daily life observed — routines, small encounters and drifting days (Paterson, Perfect Days, Wanda, Wendy and Lucy). A crisis of meaning goes to A16-8; a journey to A16-36.
leaves.see: A16-8 Existentialist Film; A16-36 Road Movie
leaves.axis: by whether the life is settled or adrift: everyday rituals, then drifters and loners

leaves.label: Chamber Drama (Kammerspiel)
leaves.defn: A drama confined to a few characters in one space or one conversation, the dialogue being the action (My Dinner with Andre, Tape, The Sunset Limited, Locke). A filmed stage production goes to A16-12 when it is about performers.
leaves.see: A16-12 Artist Film; A16-5 Domestic Drama

leaves.label: Hyperlink Cinema
leaves.defn: An ensemble drama of several separate storylines linked by chance, place or a shared event (Magnolia, 21 Grams, Babel, Crash). A single family's ensemble goes to A16-3.
leaves.see: A16-3 Family Drama; A16-19 Social Realism

leaves.label: Artist Film (Künstlerroman)
leaves.defn: A drama of a fictional artist or performer whose art or career is the engine — the actor, filmmaker, musician, writer or painter at work and in crisis (8½, All About Eve, Tár, La belle noiseuse). Real artists' lives go to A11; musicals to A14.
leaves.see: A11 Biographical Film; A14 Musical & Dance Film
leaves.axis: by the art: filmmakers first, then stage and screen performers, musicians, and writers and painters last

leaves.label: Coming-of-Age Film
leaves.defn: A drama of a child's or young adolescent's passage toward understanding, told from the child's side (The Spirit of the Beehive, My Life as a Dog, Stand by Me, Boyhood). High-school teen life goes to A16-14; delinquency to A16-15.
leaves.see: A16-14 Teen Film; A16-15 Juvenile Delinquency Film; A17 Children's & Family Film
leaves.axis: by the setting of the childhood: home and family first, then city streets, village and countryside, the summer away, childhood under war or dictatorship, and boarding school last

leaves.label: Teen Film
leaves.defn: A drama of teenage life in its own institutions — high school, cliques, first love and sexual awakening (The Breakfast Club, Lady Bird, Eighth Grade, Murmur of the Heart). Rebellion and crisis go to A16-15; teen comedies to A12; teen romance to A13.
leaves.see: A16-13 Coming-of-Age Film; A16-15 Juvenile Delinquency Film; A13 Romance
leaves.axis: by the arena of adolescence: school and friendship, then first love and sexual awakening

leaves.label: Juvenile Delinquency Film
leaves.defn: A drama of youth in revolt or in danger — gangs, rebels, subcultures and teenagers in crisis (Rebel Without a Cause, The Outsiders, This Is England, Thirteen); includes the Japanese taiyōzoku cycle (Crazed Fruit). Crime-driven youth gangs go to A2.
leaves.aliases: JD film; rebel youth film; taiyōzoku film
leaves.see: A16-14 Teen Film; A2 Crime
leaves.axis: by the form of revolt: street gangs, rebels and runaways, youth subcultures, then teenagers in crisis

leaves.label: Campus Film
leaves.defn: A drama set in a college or university, or among its just-graduated (Starter for 10, Higher Learning, St. Elmo's Fire). High school goes to A16-14; campus comedy to A12.
leaves.see: A16-14 Teen Film; A16-17 Teacher Film

leaves.label: Teacher Film
leaves.defn: A drama whose engine is a teacher and a class — the inspirational, embattled or failing educator (To Sir, with Love, Dead Poets Society, The Class, The Teachers' Lounge). Pupils' own stories go to A16-13 or A16-14.
leaves.see: A16-14 Teen Film; A16-16 Campus Film

leaves.label: LGBTQ Film
leaves.defn: A drama whose engine is queer identity — coming out, queer love and community, or trans life (Beautiful Thing, Moonlight, The Boys in the Band, A Fantastic Woman). A queer love story foregrounding romance goes to A13; the 1990s movement to A1.
leaves.aliases: queer cinema; gay and lesbian film; coming-out film
leaves.see: A1 Movements & Schools; A13 Romance; A16-14 Teen Film
leaves.axis: by the queer experience: coming out, queer love and community, then trans and intersex lives

leaves.label: Social Realism
leaves.defn: A drama of ordinary working or poor people shown in their material conditions — labour, unemployment, the street, the village (Salt of the Earth, Rosetta, I, Daniel Blake, Salaam Bombay!). A drama built around one named social issue goes to A16-22; Italian neorealism and kitchen-sink realism as movements to A1.
leaves.aliases: working-class film; kitchen-sink drama; social drama
leaves.see: A1 Movements & Schools; A16-22 Social Problem Film; A16-21 Immigrant Film
leaves.axis: by where the hardship falls: work and labour, unemployment and precarity, street life and slums, then the village

leaves.label: Banlieue Film
leaves.defn: A French drama of the multi-ethnic housing estates of the urban periphery, youth and police at its centre (La Haine, Girlhood, Les Misérables). Non-French urban dramas go to A16-19.
leaves.see: A16-19 Social Realism; A16-15 Juvenile Delinquency Film

leaves.label: Immigrant Film
leaves.defn: A drama whose engine is migration — the crossing, the arrival in a new country, or the second generation between cultures (El Norte, Minari, My Beautiful Laundrette, Io Capitano). Migration as backdrop to a crime goes to A2.
leaves.aliases: migrant cinema; diaspora film; accented cinema
leaves.see: A16-19 Social Realism; A16-36 Road Movie
leaves.axis: by the stage of migration: the arrival and new life, the second generation, then the crossing and the refugee

leaves.label: Social Problem Film
leaves.defn: A drama built to expose one named social ill — addiction, racism, sexual violence, the oppression of women, prostitution (The Lost Weekend, Gentleman's Agreement, Requiem for a Dream, Moolaadé). Diffuse working-class hardship goes to A16-19; the courtroom to A16-25.
leaves.aliases: problem picture; message film; issue film
leaves.see: A16-19 Social Realism; A16-25 Legal Drama; A16-23 Political Drama
leaves.axis: by the social ill: addictions first (drink, drugs, gambling), then race and caste, youth violence, sexual violence and reproductive rights, the oppression of women, and sex work last

leaves.label: Political Drama
leaves.defn: A drama whose engine is political power — winning and abusing office, resisting it, or living under it (Mr. Smith Goes to Washington, The Candidate, Yol, Leviathan). Political thrillers go to A3; war to A9.
leaves.see: A3 Thriller & Mystery; A16-24 Journalism Film; A9 War Film
leaves.axis: by the relation to power: holding and seeking office, activism and revolution, life under repression, then communal conflict and extremism

leaves.label: Journalism Film
leaves.defn: A drama of reporters and the press, the getting or abusing of a story being the engine (Ace in the Hole, Good Night, and Good Luck., She Said). Newspaper thrillers go to A3.
leaves.see: A16-23 Political Drama; A3 Thriller & Mystery

leaves.label: Legal Drama
leaves.defn: A drama of the law in action — the trial, the lawyer's case, the wrongful conviction (12 Angry Men, To Kill a Mockingbird, Anatomy of a Murder, Anatomy of a Fall). A whodunit with a courtroom climax goes to A3.
leaves.see: A3 Thriller & Mystery; A16-22 Social Problem Film
leaves.axis: by the kind of proceeding: the criminal trial, political and war-crimes trials, courts-martial, wrongful conviction and the death penalty, then the lawyer's civil case

leaves.label: Medical Drama
leaves.defn: A drama whose engine is illness, disability or medicine — the dying patient, the disabled life, dementia, the doctor's work (Ikiru, The Father, Scent of a Woman, Bringing Out the Dead). Mental illness as inner state goes to A16-7.
leaves.see: A16-7 Psychological Drama; A16-6 Melodrama
leaves.axis: by the condition: doctors and carers, terminal illness, disability, then dementia

leaves.label: Religious Drama
leaves.defn: A drama whose engine is faith — the priest's or nun's vocation, doubt, conversion or fanaticism (Diary of a Country Priest, Winter Light, Ida, First Reformed). Evangelical industry films go to A16-28; biblical epics to A8.
leaves.aliases: faith drama; spiritual film; transcendental style
leaves.see: A16-28 Christian Film; A8 Historical & Period Film
leaves.axis: by who carries the faith: priests and pastors, nuns and convents, then lay believers and seekers

leaves.label: Christian Film
leaves.defn: A film made by or for the evangelical Christian film industry, whose plot affirms faith (Fireproof, God's Not Dead, The Shack); includes the early race-film religious dramas (The Blood of Jesus). Art-house faith dramas go to A16-27.
leaves.see: A16-27 Religious Drama

leaves.label: Sports Film
leaves.defn: A drama whose engine is athletic contest outside the sports given their own leaves — ice and snow, field games, golf and racket sports, athletics, gymnastics, boards, racing animals and bicycles, cue games and combat sports (Chariots of Fire, The Hustler, Miracle, Lagaan). Boxing, baseball, American football, basketball, football and motor racing have leaves A16-30 to A16-35.
leaves.see: A16-30 Boxing Film; A12 Comedy
leaves.axis: by the sport: ice and snow first, then field games, golf and racket sports, running and swimming, gymnastics and cheer, board sports, horse and bicycle racing, cue and table games, and combat sports last

leaves.label: Boxing Film
leaves.defn: A sports drama of the prizefighter and the ring, including cage fighting (Rocky, Fat City, Million Dollar Baby, Creed).
leaves.see: A16-29 Sports Film

leaves.label: Baseball Film
leaves.defn: A sports drama of baseball (The Pride of the Yankees, The Natural, Bull Durham, Moneyball).
leaves.see: A16-29 Sports Film

leaves.label: American Football Film
leaves.defn: A sports drama of American (gridiron) football (Rudy, Remember the Titans, Friday Night Lights, Any Given Sunday).
leaves.see: A16-29 Sports Film

leaves.label: Basketball Film
leaves.defn: A sports drama of basketball (Hoosiers, He Got Game, Coach Carter, Love & Basketball).
leaves.see: A16-29 Sports Film

leaves.label: Association Football Film
leaves.defn: A sports drama of association football (Victory, Bend It Like Beckham, Goal! The Dream Begins, Next Goal Wins).
leaves.see: A16-29 Sports Film

leaves.label: Auto Racing Film
leaves.defn: A sports drama of motor racing (Grand Prix, Le Mans, Rush, Ford v Ferrari).
leaves.see: A16-29 Sports Film; A7 Action & Martial Arts

leaves.label: Road Movie
leaves.defn: A drama whose engine is the journey itself — leaving home, the open road and what it changes (Wild Strawberries, Thelma & Louise, The Straight Story, Nomadland). A journey driven by the bond of two friends goes to A16-37; migrant crossings to A16-21.
leaves.see: A16-37 Buddy Film; A16-21 Immigrant Film
leaves.axis: by who travels and why: the family trip, lovers and outlaws on the run, motorcycle journeys, pilgrimages on foot, quests of search and memory, then drifters and nomads

leaves.label: Buddy Film
leaves.defn: A film whose engine is the friendship of two (or a small band of) companions, here mostly on a trip together (Planes, Trains & Automobiles, Rain Man, Y tu mamá también, The Trip). Cop-buddy action goes to A7; pure road comedy also to A12.
leaves.aliases: buddy road movie; female buddy film
leaves.see: A16-36 Road Movie; A12 Comedy; A7 Action & Martial Arts
leaves.axis: by the pairing: male friends, female friends, mismatched pairs, then groups of friends

leaves.label: Animal Film
leaves.defn: A drama whose engine is the bond between people and an animal, or an animal's own odyssey (Lassie Come Home, The Black Stallion, Au hasard Balthazar, Hachi: A Dog's Tale). Animated talking-animal films go to C12; wildlife documentary to A19.
leaves.see: A17 Children's & Family Film; A19 Documentary
leaves.axis: by the animal: dogs first, then horses, then wild and farm animals
